notes.phase: render-reel.mjs indexes a bg.sequence from the scene's local time (frame = floor(local x 30) mod 300), so each later card would restart the orbit. Workaround (renderer untouched): production/assets/loop-spacetime/phase/<seq>-<k> are the same sequences rotated by k frames (symlinks, make-phase-dirs.sh); k = the card's global start frame mod 300, so card N shows global frame (start + local) and the orbit runs continuously across the cuts: card 2 k=180, card 3 k=60 (360 mod 300), card 4 k=240 (540), card 5 k=120 (720). Cards run 0 to 30.0 s = 900 frames = exactly three orbits, so the last card frame (899, phase 299) leads into the end card (phase 0 still) and the loop returns to card 1 frame 0 (phase 0). This is why the cards end at 30.0 s and not the script's 30.5 s: 30.5 s would put the seam 15 frames off phase. Total 31.5 s.

caption:
If nothing pulls Earth, why does it not fly off? (It coasts on the straightest path through space-time the Sun has curved, and that path closes into an orbit.)
Einstein, Die Feldgleichungen der Gravitation, Prussian Academy, 25 Nov 1915. Dyson, Eddington and Davidson, 1919 eclipse results, Royal Society, 6 Nov 1919.

Newton's textbook picture is a force tugging across empty space. Einstein's is geometry: mass curves space-time and free objects follow its straightest lines. Einstein predicted starlight grazing the Sun bends by 1.75 arcseconds, twice Newton's value. Two expeditions measured it at the 29 May 1919 eclipse and got his number. The dented grid is a 2D analogy of 4D curvature. Images are generated illustrations.

#gravity #physics #einstein #science
